source.title: Dynamics of Gradient Descent with Large Step Size Near a Manifold of Flat Minima

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes and numerically illustrates large-step gradient descent in overparameterized least-squares matrix factorization, a different setting from the neural-network training dynamics in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper's results concern convergence dynamics near a manifold of flat minima, not CIFAR classification error. Its figures report iterate norms and distance to the flat-minima manifold; it does not report training loss or sharpness trajectories. Other claim versions are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes local convergence near flat-minima manifolds. Its thresholds use sharpness on that manifold, and its experiments measure iterate coordinates rather than V5's loss and curvature dynamics relative to the initial linearized model. Section 6 explicitly places progressive sharpening and edge-of-stability dynamics outside its results, except potentially their tail end.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors extend local large-step gradient-descent theory to vector-valued least squares and manifolds of flat minima, establish three convergence regimes, and verify them numerically in deep matrix factorization. They explicitly say their results do not address convergence away from that manifold or the earlier progressive-sharpening and edge-of-stability regimes.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of gradient descent on overparameterized least-squares matrix factorization near flat-minima manifolds; not classification-network benchmark training.
record.method_sensitivity: Behavior depends on whether the step size is subcritical, critical, or supercritical relative to 2/λ1|F.

fits_no_version.finding: Five trials in each regime illustrate exponential convergence to a suboptimally flat minimum, polynomial convergence to F, or exponential attraction to a period-two orbit, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Near a flat-minima manifold satisfying the stated geometric assumptions, least-squares gradient descent has three local convergence regimes determined by the step size relative to 2/λ1 on F.

record.problems: Numerical evidence is limited to five independent trials on a 3-layer, 2 × 2 matrix-factorization problem. The theorems are local to a neighborhood of the flat-minima manifold; loss and sharpness trajectories are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No results meeting the row criteria were left out. The paper's theoretical convergence theorems are not separate empirical rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and recipe-dependent exceptions.
Spurious-minimum frequency and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Loss rise, curvature reduction and recovery relative to the initial linearized-model threshold; divergence at larger rates; progressive sharpening and sustained edge-of-stability dynamics; divergence from below the initial threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Sections 4–5 and Appendix D prove local sharpness descent and convergence results, but these do not establish the specific trajectories named in V5. The theoretical results were already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing rows. No verdict is warranted merely from this difference in scope.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, training duration, and early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima frequency, and student width.
Plain versus residual convolutional network training error and depth.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.

The study does not measure loss or sharpness trajectories, compare learning rates to the initial linearized-model stability limit, or test the cited neural-network settings. Its results are local to least-squares problems near flat minima.
Batch-normalization comparisons, training speed, accuracy, and learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: 3 layer, 2 × 2 matrix factorisation problem
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent in the subcritical regime; five independent trials shown.
rows.measure: Iterate norm and distance to the flat-minima manifold over iterations.
rows.value: All trials show initial instability followed by exponential convergence to a suboptimally flat minimum.
rows.note: The figure caption describes both plotted measures and the convergence outcome; it does not report loss or sharpness.
rows.check: The reported transient is growth in the normal-coordinate norm, followed by convergence. It does not establish V5's initial loss rise and curvature drop above the initial linearized-model stability limit. The caption's outcome is otherwise accurately recorded.

rows.subject: 3 layer, 2 × 2 matrix factorisation problem
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent in the critical regime; five independent trials shown.
rows.measure: Iterate norm and distance to the flat-minima manifold over iterations.
rows.value: All trials exhibit the predicted asymptotic t−1/2 convergence to an element of F.
rows.note: The caption reports iterate convergence, not loss or sharpness.
rows.check: Polynomial convergence at a threshold defined by sharpness on F does not measure V5's recovery or sharpness rising to and hovering at the stability threshold.

rows.subject: 3 layer, 2 × 2 matrix factorisation problem
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent in the supercritical regime; five independent trials shown.
rows.measure: Iterate norm and distance to the flat-minima manifold over iterations.
rows.value: All trials exhibit exponential convergence to the claimed period-2 cycle along ν1 |F.
rows.note: The caption reports convergence to a period-two orbit; it does not report loss or sharpness.
rows.check: Convergence to a period-two orbit slightly above the threshold on F does not measure V5's initial instability and recovery, sustained edge-of-stability dynamics, or divergence at larger rates.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The paper discusses progressive sharpening and edge-of-stability dynamics, but Section 6 explicitly places them beyond its local results except at their tail end.

tranche.reason: Local convergence near a flat-minima manifold and normal-coordinate dynamics do not establish any claim version. V5's loss and sharpness trajectories relative to the initial linearized-model threshold are not tested.

source_check.notes: The plotted norm is the normal-coordinate norm, not the full parameter norm. Regime thresholds use sharpness on F; the authors' stated conclusions and local-convergence limitation match the record.
